name: Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
history: One of the 12 sacred Jyotirlingas, Omkareshwar is situated on an island shaped like the Hindu symbol OM on the Narmada river. The temple has two shrines — Omkareshwar and Amareshwar.
history_hindi: ओंकारेश्वर 12 ज्योतिर्लिंगों में से एक है जो नर्मदा नदी पर OM आकार के द्वीप पर स्थित है।
sthala_purana: Lord Brahma and Vishnu had a dispute over superiority. Shiva appeared as an infinite pillar of light. The island itself took the shape of the sacred OM.
significance: The island temple sits in the middle of the Narmada river and its natural OM shape makes it supremely sacred. A visit here is said to grant moksha.
puranic_stories: King Mandhata performed severe penance on this island to please Lord Shiva. The island itself is shaped like the Hindu sacred syllable OM when viewed from above.

name: Mamleshwar Temple
history: Mamleshwar is the second shrine of the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga complex located across the river. Together they constitute the single Jyotirlinga of Omkareshwar.
history_hindi: मामलेश्वर ओंकारेश्वर के दूसरे तीर्थ हैं जो नदी के पार स्थित हैं।
sthala_purana: The two parts of the single Jyotirlinga — Omkareshwar on the island and Mamleshwar on the south bank together form the complete sacred pilgrimage.
significance: The second part of the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga. Many devotees are unaware that the complete Jyotirlinga darshan requires visiting both temples.
puranic_stories: Amareshwar is named after the gods (Amar=immortal) who worshipped Shiva here after the demon Mandhata's defeat.

name: Pashupatinath Temple Mandsaur
history: The Pashupatinath temple in Mandsaur houses a rare 8-faced Shivalinga called the Ashta-Mukhi Shivalinga. This is one of the most unique Shivalingas in India.
history_hindi: मंदसौर का पशुपतिनाथ मंदिर अष्टमुखी शिवलिंग के लिए प्रसिद्ध है जो भारत में अत्यंत दुर्लभ है।
sthala_purana: The 8-faced Shivalinga is believed to have been carved in the Gupta period. Each face represents a different manifestation of Lord Shiva.
significance: Houses the extremely rare 8-faced Shivalinga. Each face of the linga represents a different form of Lord Shiva, found nowhere else in India.
puranic_stories: The Ashta-Mukhi Shivalinga was discovered during excavations and is believed to be a self-manifested sacred object from the Gupta era.

name: Pitambara Peeth
history: Pitambara Peeth is one of the most powerful Shakti shrines in India. The goddess Baglamukhi is worshipped here and the temple is famous for powerful tantric rituals.
history_hindi: पीताम्बरा पीठ भारत के सबसे शक्तिशाली शक्ति मंदिरों में से एक है।
sthala_purana: Baglamukhi is one of the 10 Mahavidyas. The goddess can paralyze enemies and grant victory. The yellow-clad deity is worshipped with yellow flowers, haldi, and yellow garments.
significance: One of India's most powerful Shakti shrines. Famous for Havan rituals. Highly visited by powerful people before elections and court cases. Rare Dhumavati temple also present.
puranic_stories: Dhumavati — the widowed form of the goddess — has her shrine here, making Pitambara Peeth one of very few places where she is enshrined.

name: Shri Ram Raja Temple
history: The only temple in India where Lord Ram is worshipped as a King and receives a royal gun salute daily. Ram was brought here as an idol by Queen Ganeshi Bai.
history_hindi: यह भारत का एकमात्र मंदिर है जहां भगवान राम को राजा के रूप में पूजा जाता है।
sthala_purana: Queen Ganeshi Bai of Orchha brought the Ram idol from Ayodhya but it refused to move from her palace. The palace was converted into a temple.
significance: The ONLY temple in India where Lord Ram is worshipped as a King and receives police salute. The idol is treated as the reigning king of Orchha.
puranic_stories: Ram Raja is considered the actual King of Orchha. The police guard changes at the temple gate daily just like a royal palace.

name: Chaturbhuj Temple Orchha
history: Chaturbhuj temple was originally built to house the Ram idol that now resides in Ram Raja temple. It has a unique combination of temple and fort architecture.
history_hindi: चतुर्भुज मंदिर मूलतः उस राम प्रतिमा के लिए बनाया गया था जो अब राम राजा मंदिर में है।
sthala_purana: When Queen Ganeshi Bai's idol of Ram chose to stay in the palace, this magnificent temple was left without its deity. Later Vishnu was installed here.
significance: Architecturally stunning — the only temple in India that combines temple architecture with fort design. Has a massive 344-step staircase with breathtaking views.
puranic_stories: The temple's massive platform was designed to accommodate lakhs of devotees and the idol was to be enshrined at a great height as befitting royalty.

name: Bijasan Mata Temple
history: Bijasan Mata temple is located on a hill in Indore and is the presiding deity of the city. The temple sees massive footfall during Navratri.
history_hindi: बिजासन माता मंदिर इंदौर शहर की अधिष्ठात्री देवी का मंदिर है।
sthala_purana: Goddess Bijasan is the city goddess of Indore and has been worshipped since the Holkar dynasty. She is believed to protect the entire city from harm.
significance: The presiding deity of Indore city. Offers panoramic views. During Navratri the temple is decorated with over 10000 lamps creating a breathtaking sight.
puranic_stories: Bijasan is a form of the divine mother Durga who guards the city from atop the hill. The hill itself is considered sacred.

name: Kanch Mandir Indore
history: Kanch Mandir is a stunning Jain temple built entirely of glass mirrors. Every surface — walls, ceiling, pillars, floors — is covered with intricate mirror mosaic work. Built by Seth Hukumchand.
history_hindi: काँच मंदिर पूरी तरह से काँच की पच्चीकारी से बना एक अनूठा जैन मंदिर है।
sthala_purana: Seth Hukumchand built this temple as a religious offering. The entire interior is covered with colored Belgian glass mirror work.
significance: One of the most visually spectacular temples in India. Every single surface covered in multicolored glass and mirrors. The effect when light hits is absolutely magical.
puranic_stories: Jain temples represent the perfection of the universe. The glass and mirror work symbolizes the infinite reflections of the soul's journey toward moksha.

name: Khajrana Ganesh Temple
history: Khajrana Ganesh is the most visited temple in Indore with thousands of devotees daily. The Ganesha idol here is said to be swayambhu (self-manifested). Ahilyabai Holkar is believed to have discovered the idol.
history_hindi: खजराना गणेश इंदौर का सबसे अधिक दर्शनीय मंदिर है जहाँ प्रतिदिन हजारों श्रद्धालु आते हैं।
sthala_purana: The swayambhu Ganesha was discovered by queen Ahilyabai Holkar during excavation. She built a grand temple around the idol.
significance: Most visited temple in Indore. The self-manifested Ganesha is believed to fulfill all wishes. The ladoo prasad is legendary. On Wednesdays the queue can be hours long.
puranic_stories: Lord Ganesha is the remover of obstacles. The swayambhu idol at Khajrana is especially powerful because it is self-manifested — not made by human hands.

name: Annapurna Temple Indore
history: Annapurna temple in Indore is famous for housing replicas of the Kashi Vishwanath Shivalinga. Built so that elderly devotees who cannot travel to Varanasi can get the same darshan in Indore.
history_hindi: इंदौर का अन्नपूर्णा मंदिर काशी विश्वनाथ की प्रतिकृति के साथ बनाया गया है।
sthala_purana: Goddess Annapurna is the goddess of food and nourishment. She resides in Kashi. This temple brings Kashi to Indore.
significance: A gift to devotees who cannot travel to Kashi. Houses authentic replicas of Kashi Vishwanath. Famous for free prasad distribution.
puranic_stories: Annapurna feeds the entire world. Kashi is her city. By building this temple in Indore the founders brought the blessings of Kashi to central India.

name: Bawangaja Jain Temple
history: Bawangaja houses the tallest Jain idol in the world — a 84-foot monolithic statue of Lord Adinath carved from a single rock.
history_hindi: बावनगजा में विश्व की सबसे ऊँची जैन प्रतिमा 84 फुट की है।
sthala_purana: The rock-cut Adinath statue is considered one of the greatest Jain pilgrimage sites. Bawangaja means 52 yards — the height of the idol.
significance: Home to the WORLD'S TALLEST Jain idol — 84 feet carved from a single rock. A hidden gem requiring a forest trek to reach.
puranic_stories: Lord Adinath (Rishabhadeva) is the first Tirthankara of Jains. The idol here has stood for centuries as a beacon of the Jain faith.
